mechanism.name: Yang--Tokdar univariate quantile-plane DGP: conditional 0.9 quantile at X=0.5

generation_equations.label: Published Section 5.1 predictor, PDF p.8 / JASA p.1113, unnumbered
Published Section 5.1 conditional quantile, PDF p.8 / JASA p.1113, unnumbered
Derived sampling representation, not an added noise law
generation_equations.expression: U ~ Uniform(0,1), independent of X; Y=Q_Y(U|X); iid pairs across rows; only X,Y observed/exported

sampling.unit: one fully observed pair (X,Y) from the synthetic population
sampling.dependence: iid rows; X and Y are dependent within a row. Internal U_i independent of X_i and across units. No latent variable is exported.

assumptions: Independent identically distributed rows (X_i,Y_i); stochastic predictor design X_i uniform(-1,1). Published Section 4 PDF p.7/journal1112 specifies independent predictor draws; Section 2.3 PDF p.5/journal1110 gives the likelihood. iid joint realization and independent inverse-transform uniforms are explicit here; published Eq.(2) PDF p.2/journal1107 gives the sampling representation.
Complete observation of X and Y without selection, censoring, missingness, clusters, panels, interference or additional measurement error in the published Section 5.1 univariate simulation.

X has positive density 1/2 near the interior query x=0.5. Because a single continuous-X point has probability zero, use the smooth conditional-law version fixed by the model; do not identify an arbitrary point-version without regularity.

The stated quantile function is differentiable and strictly increasing in tau for every x in [-1,1], tends to minus/plus infinity at the endpoints and yields a continuous positive conditional density at the target; analytic proof in card.

Only regularity needed to define the scalar truth is asserted. Bayesian-prior conditions of the paper are not additional DGP parameters. No causal intervention, exchangeability or mediation assumptions apply.

properties.notes: One observed input X, active because beta_1(0.9)=0.64*log(100/9) is nonzero. Quantile planes are affine in X for each tau, so nonlinear=false uses the observed-covariate-surface convention. Coefficient curves are nonlinear in tau: beta_0=3(tau-1/2)log[1/(tau(1-tau))], beta_1=4(tau-1/2)^2 log[1/(tau(1-tau))]; this is recorded but not called nonlinear in X. No observed X_j*X_k term, hence interactions=false; latent-rank modulation is not an extra observed covariate interaction. p=1 vs check n=128, not high dimensional.

estimand.name: theta = Q_Y(0.9 | X=0.5)
estimand.definition: inf{y: F_Y(y | X=0.5) >= 0.9} under the source superpopulation; use the conditional distribution version continuous in x specified by the quantile-plane law. A noncausal scalar conditional quantile, not a marginal quantile, beta_1(0.9), prediction interval, or simultaneous band.

truth.expression: inf{y: F_Y(y | X=0.5) >= 0.9} under the source superpopulation; use the conditional distribution version continuous in x specified by the quantile-plane law. A noncausal scalar conditional quantile, not a marginal quantile, beta_1(0.9), prediction interval, or simultaneous band.
truth.derivation: Analytic theta=(38/25)*log(100/9), Decimal 50/80 precision and float-rounding audit; independent numerical integration of the quantile derivative from the zero median, plus CDF inversion and analytic special cases.

adaptations: Retain the complete published Section 5.1 quantile law, X~Uniform(-1,1), coefficients 3 and 4, center 1/2 and powers. Choose query_x=0.5 and quantile_level=0.9 for the scalar Arena target; this query and numeric result are collection adaptations, not a single-point result designated or reported by the paper.

Implement this conditional law by Y=Q(U|X), U uniform(0,1) independent of X, using local Python Random(seed) and iid rows. This is an independent law-equivalent implementation, not author-code or original-dataset replay; the published Section 5.1 experiment script, commit and author RNG/seed have not been located.

Output observed X,Y only. Finite-precision random() draws reject u=0 and use stable logarithms; no arbitrary tail clipping, extra noise or changed coefficient. Local seed and finite PRNG support are implementation choices.

Check n=128, seed=1729 rather than rerun the paper experiments (100 datasets of n=1000), estimators, MCMC, bootstrap or coverage. Analytic special cases are diagnostics within one declared scenario, not new mechanisms.

Retain source-only audit evidence dated 2026-10-31 for the supplement, published main text, pinned GitHub estimator snapshot and observed CRAN documentation. Do not import estimator preprocessing, example noise, censoring or base distributions into the DGP.
